You'll make these critical systems stronger, more reliable, and more capable, while building the next generation of them and the infrastructure that lets a small team move fast on systems that handle real money. Your work is visible across the whole company, and you'll have the flexibility to take on greenfield projects that make the entire engineering team more productive. Design for correctness, durability, and auditability across every processor and product we run on. - Protect players and the platform. Build the anti-fraud enforcement, dispute handling, and player-trust systems that keep real-money gaming fair, and give support and operations the tooling to act on them. - Scale core systems through hypergrowth. jobs.description_text: The Role Rips is our collectibles trading card app, it lives on mobile, and it is growing fast. You'll be building it. This is the product, not a port of it. Our app is React Native and Expo. You’ll be shipping to real users who are trading real value, which means correctness, latency, and polish are not separable concerns here. A dropped state update is not a cosmetic bug when there is money on the other side of it. You'll own significant surface area from day one: features end to end, the interaction quality that makes them feel native, and the technical decisions underneath. We're a small team, so the person who designs something is the person who ships it and the person who owns it afterward. What You'll Do - Build and own core product features in React Native and Expo, from design discussion through launch and iteration. - Take the user experience seriously: motion, gesture, transitions, perceived performance, and the small details that separate an app people tolerate from one they open every day. - Go below the abstraction when the problem requires it. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE: Team's mission Upvest's core product is an API: the execution layer that moves securities for our clients. Upfront extends into the layer above it. It's Upvest's operational service panel for enterprise clients, giving their operations, support and compliance staff the ability to handle first-line requests themselves: looking into an end-user's account, checking what happened to an order, answering the question in front of them. Today their options are to ask Upvest support or to build a service panel of their own, which most of them won't do. Our mission is to prove that financial institution customers can replace their fragmented operations with Upfront. That case isn't settled yet, and this team is the one making it. Our users do this work all day, so a clumsy interface is how a task turns back into a ticket for us. Our clients are already asking what AI can do for their operations teams. Agentic operations, exposed over MCP, is where we think this goes. What it should look like in Upfront is still open, and we'd like the person in this role to help define it. Upfront is part of the Clients Tribe at Upvest. Together with the Public API and Tooling Apps teams we enable Upvest’s business to scale efficiently, accelerate our client’s time-to-market and embed intelligence and automation into client processes. jobs.title: Flight Software Engineer
jobs.description_text: At The Exploration Company we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx - a modular, reusable orbital vehicle for space missions to stations and beyond. Nyx is engineered with the capability to transport cargo and, in the future, humans. We are seeking a highly motivated Flight Software Engineer to join our mission-driven team developing Nyx. In this role, you will take full ownership of key components of the flight software stack. You will be designing, implementing, and testing mission-critical systems that enable safe, autonomous, and reliable spaceflight operations. You will work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment where cross-functional integration is essential. Your code will interface directly with vehicle avionics, guidance systems, propulsion, communications, and ground control. Expect to write modern, high-reliability C++ and Python code, drive software simulations, and ensure flight readiness through rigorous testing at both unit and system levels. The position level will be determined based on your experience, technical depth, and ability to take ownership. jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description_text: WindBorne is an atypical hardware company: we sell the data our balloons produce, not the balloons. Our customer is our own operations team, which puts engineering and the field about as close together as they can get. We push design changes to flying hardware roughly once a week while scaling production at the same time. Today every part of that loop is owned by full-stack engineers who each design a part, own its tooling, and tweak it based on field performance. That has worked so far, but manufacturing throughput and tooling maintenance have grown into a full-time load that can no longer share a desk with design iteration. This role exists to take that load. Manufacturing and Production turns engineering designs into repeatable, high-quality production. We build mechatronic hardware assemblies — PCBA, electronic sensors, ballast, and an adjustable inflatable balloon. Boards arrive populated from our suppliers. On our floor, we assemble the PCBAs into the electronics assembly, test it, and then build up the mechanical hardware, ballast, and balloon around it. The work is manual to semi-automated, and it has to hold together while the designs underneath it keep changing. We are running about 1,000 units a month and doubling roughly every six months. Most hardware teams get design lock before volume. We don't, and the manufacturing system has to work anyway. Own manufacturing engineering for parts as they come off the design team. jobs.title: Estate Planning Specialist, Wealth Management
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE This is the first role of its kind at Wealthsimple. As our Estate Planning Specialist, you'll build the foundation of how we review and optimize estate plans for our Wealth Management clients — an area that many HNW clients fail to properly address, even when the rest of their financial plan is sound. You'll join a growing specialist bench that already includes our Tax Planning team and our Family Enterprise Advisor. Like those functions, your job isn't to draft legal documents or sell products — it's to review clients' existing wills, trust documents, and broader estate plans, identify where they no longer align with (or never accounted for) the client's actual goals, and clearly explain in plain language what needs to change and who can help make that happen. This is not a sales role and will not be selling insurance, or anything else. Your job is to advocate for the client's best interests — identifying gaps and misalignments, and connecting clients to the right resource to solve them, whether that's our estate lawyer referral network, our documentation-drafting partners. As the newest Specialist to the team, you won't just be executing an established process — you'll be responsible for helping design and build the estate review and planning process itself, in partnership with the Wealth Management leadership team. jobs.description_text: About the Team Our team is at the core of Avride's self-driving stack. We build the base infrastructure layer that powers all autopilot code. It includes a C++ framework for implementing autonomy components, execution graph building and optimization systems, as well as runtimes that execute those graphs, both onboard and in simulation. It is the first priority within this role. jobs.department: Autonomous Vehicles / Motion planning / Offline testing
jobs.description_text: About the team Avride builds autonomous driving technology for vehicles and delivery robots, and tests it on public roads in Austin. Before anything reaches those roads it goes through our QA team: checks on every pull request, a daily validation of main, and release-candidate qualification over a large set of recorded scenes. Every one of those gates produces a verdict, and the safety part of that verdict is the one people act on. About the role You will own how safety is tested, judged and reported across our QA team. Our Head of Safety owns the company's safety framework and the safety case built on top of it. You own the layer beneath: the gates, the criteria and the reports that turn day-to-day testing into evidence that argument can rest on. The hard part of this is not the collisions. Those are obvious, and nobody argues about them. It is everything short of a collision the near miss, the late brake, the hesitation at an intersection that looked wrong to one engineer and fine to another where the judgement has to be made and then made the same way again next week, by someone else, on a different run. Turning that into criteria a whole team applies consistently is the craft of this role. You will lead through process and through people who do not report to you. What you’ll do Own the safety gates.
